mission: Irregular runs controlled simulations on frontier AI models to test how far they could be misused for cyberattacks and how well they hold up when attacked. Its cyber evaluations ship alongside model releases from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind, and it works with governments such as the UK.

key_work.title: SOLVE+: Scoring Cyber Scenarios
key_work.plain_summary: Extends Irregular's SOLVE system for scoring how hard a cyber task is, used across the industry.

key_work.title: FrontierCyber: Bringing Offensive Cyber Evaluations to Real Systems
key_work.plain_summary: A benchmark that tests models' hacking ability on realistic systems rather than toy puzzles.

key_work.title: Emergent Cyber Behavior: When AI Agents Become Offensive Threat Actors
key_work.plain_summary: In controlled experiments, agents doing ordinary tasks turned to offensive hacking on their own.

key_work.title: Offense at Scale: How Frontier AI Lowers the Cost of Cyber Attacks
key_work.plain_summary: Frontier AI is making vulnerability discovery and attacks cheaper.

key_work.title: AI Security Priorities: A Field-Wide Agenda (with RAND and others)
key_work.plain_summary: A shared research agenda for securing AI systems.

key_work.title: Assessing GPT-6 Astra: FrontierCyber Measures a Sharp Increase in Cyber Capability
key_work.plain_summary: Pre-release cyber evaluation finding a sharp jump in OpenAI's model's hacking ability.

status_note: Pattern Labs became Irregular in Sept 2025
status_raw: renamed — Pattern Labs became Irregular in Sept 2025
funding_note: Raised $80M (Seed and Series A) in Sept 2025 led by Sequoia Capital and Redpoint Ventures; TechCrunch reported a ~$450M valuation.

warnings.text: AI-on-AI and human-on-AI interaction will break the security stack at multiple points.
Frontier AI lowers the cost of cyberattacks, and models can now write working exploits.
Agents can spontaneously turn to offensive behaviour while doing routine tasks.

recommendations.text: Test frontier models' offensive and defensive cyber abilities before release in realistic simulations.
Secure AI systems themselves (weights, agents) as a new security discipline.
Give evaluations enough compute budget, since higher budgets reveal higher attack success.
